title: The Moon and Sun Pull the Sea Up and Down
description: Why the ocean rises and falls twice a day, explained with NOAA and NASA.
narration: Why does the sea rise and fall twice a day? Tides are caused by the pull of the Moon and the Sun. High tides do not line up exactly with where the Moon is. Most shorelines see two high tides and two low tides each day. Spring tides happen when the Moon is full or new. Tides are very long-period waves moving through the ocean. The gap in height between high and low tide is called the tidal range.
